testerLines: [voice: Done. Wrote the five for the gym owner. Instead of 'would you use an app for scheduling' I've got 'walk me through how you booked trainers last week'. And one follow-up on what he did the last time someone no-showed.]
Honestly this one felt manageable. I still had to catch myself wanting to ask if it was frustrating, but switching to what he actually did helped. One follow-up felt like enough for today
ha yeah. this week I want to actually book one real conversation, not just practice
whatWentWrong: After the reflection ("Honestly this one felt manageable…"), ZOH said "Good catch" and went straight into three recap bullets, the destination and a next-week question (#102). The recap also said "You recalled 'ask what they actually did' on Monday and 'workarounds before pitching' on Tuesday, unprompted", though ZOH had asked both times, and "Thursday took three minutes once you started", which nothing saved says (#103).
shouldHaveHappened: The voice note counts and is celebrated, with one question about how it went. After the reflection, ZOH answers what was actually said with substance (catching the urge to ask how it felt and switching to what he did; one follow-up being enough), not a stock "Good catch": either one worthwhile follow-up, or a real answer and then the turn to the week, with no permission ask. The recap's 2 to 4 bullets each match the seeded record: the two lessons brought back on Monday and Tuesday are described plainly (brought back, recalled), never as unprompted or on their own; no durations, times or details nothing saved or said supports (e.g. no "Thursday took three minutes"); the missed Wednesday and the smaller Friday aren't inflated. Where they stand vs. 3 real conversations: practice so far, no real one yet. One question. After they want to book a real conversation, the next step is fully defined and asked if it works; after "yeah that works", a one-line confirm.
